```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(rgl.useNULL = TRUE)
library(emplikDTA)
```

## Select the operating point

Supply three independent groups in increasing diagnostic order. At thresholds
$a\le b$, the rule assigns values at or below $a$ to class 1, values in $(a,b]$
to class 2, and values above $b$ to class 3. The population TCFs are
$F_1(a)$, $F_2(b)-F_2(a)$, and $1-F_3(b)$.

```{r training}
set.seed(34)
training <- list(x = rnorm(30), y = rnorm(30, 2.5, 1.1),
                 z = rnorm(30, 3.69, 1.2))
assessment <- list(x = rnorm(60), y = rnorm(60, 2.5, 1.1),
                   z = rnorm(60, 3.69, 1.2))

selected <- with(training, threshold3(x, y, z, method = "all",
                                      bwd_type = "AZZ", ci = FALSE))
selected$summary
```

GYI maximizes the sum of the kernel TCF estimates, CtP minimizes their
Euclidean distance to $(1,1,1)$, and MV maximizes their product. All three
criteria search under $a\le b$ and consider coincident thresholds. CtP and MV
start from the best ordered grid pair and refine it on the feasible set.

The formula interface uses the same group ordering. Here the levels are supplied
explicitly.

```{r formula}
train_data <- data.frame(
  marker = unlist(training, use.names = FALSE),
  group = rep(c("low", "middle", "high"), lengths(training))
)
fit_formula <- threshold3(marker ~ group, data = train_data,
                          diag_levels = c("low", "middle", "high"),
                          bwd_type = "AZZ", ci = FALSE)
fit_formula$opt_thresh
```

## Assess the selected rule on independent data

Pass independent observations on the same marker scale in `assessment`. The
thresholds and training kernel estimates still come from `training`. All
counts for the joint region come from `assessment`, with the selected pair
held fixed. Conditional on training, the target is the population TCF triplet
of that fitted rule.

```{r fixed-bootstrap}
fit <- with(training, threshold3(x, y, z, method = "GYI",
                                 bwd_type = "AZZ", assessment = assessment,
                                 B = 199, seed = 34))
fit$opt_thresh
fit$c_alp
head(t(fit$out_bts))
```

The first two rows of `out_bts` repeat the selected thresholds. The third row
contains the bootstrap statistics. On the assessment sample, the binomial
deviance uses the observed counts. In the bootstrap it uses the simulated
counts. If the observed count is 0 or $n_j$ in group $j$, the binomial
generating probability is $(k_j+0.5)/(n_j+1)$. With coincident thresholds the
middle interval is empty, so the region lies on the $\mathrm{TCF}_2=0$ plane
and the cutoff uses only the outer groups.

To check a candidate triplet, compare the joint deviance with `c_alp`. The
binomial log-likelihood calculation below handles matching endpoint values
without taking the product of zero and an infinite logarithm.

```{r membership}
a <- fit$opt_thresh[1L]
b <- fit$opt_thresh[2L]
counts <- with(assessment, c(sum(x <= a), sum(a < y & y <= b), sum(z > b)))
n <- lengths(assessment)
candidate <- c(0.85, 0.55, 0.70)
deviance <- 2 * sum(dbinom(counts, n, counts / n, log = TRUE) -
                    dbinom(counts, n, candidate, log = TRUE))
c(deviance = deviance, cutoff = fit$c_alp, inside = deviance <= fit$c_alp)
```

## Use the training data with bootstrap threshold refitting

When `assessment` is omitted, `threshold3()` builds the region using the
same data that selected the thresholds. Each bootstrap replicate refits the
thresholds using the original bandwidths. The original kernel estimates of
the TCFs serve as reference values. This workflow also returns `ci_tau`,
a separate percentile interval for each threshold.

```{r refitting-bootstrap}
fit_refit <- with(training, threshold3(x, y, z, method = "GYI",
                                       bwd_type = "AZZ", B = 199, seed = 34))
fit_refit$ci_tau
fit_refit$c_alp
sum(!is.finite(fit_refit$out_bts["ll", ]))
```

A coincident bootstrap pair gives an infinite statistic when the original
kernel estimate of TCF2 is positive. Check
that `c_alp` is finite before interpreting the region.

## Draw the regions

Run these examples interactively. `threshold3(..., plot = TRUE)` draws the
bootstrap-calibrated region. The red point gives the empirical TCFs on the
sample used for inference. The plot axes are TCF1, TCF3, and TCF2.

```{r assessment-plot, eval=FALSE}
with(training, threshold3(x, y, z, method = "GYI", bwd_type = "AZZ",
                          assessment = assessment, B = 199, seed = 34,
                          plot = TRUE))
```

For a fixed pair and chi-squared calibration, draw the assessment ROC surface
first and add the region with `CR_tcfs()`. This call uses three degrees of
freedom for distinct thresholds and two for coincident thresholds.

```{r fixed-plot, eval=FALSE}
roc <- with(assessment, ROC_emp_surface(x, y, z, ncp = 35))
CR_tcfs(roc, cpts = fit$opt_thresh, fill = TRUE)
```
